decisions.reason: The broadened editorial approval gate does not change the manuscript word limit or chapter-allocation rules.
The chapter was expressly included by the client; the approval gate for proposed content changes does not alter its topic, format, or question-count rule.
The client-approved chapter remains required with unchanged format and allocation rules; the separate approval workflow does not modify those attributes.
The approval gate does not change the already authorized chapter topic, question-and-answer format, or word-budget-dependent question policy.
Editorial approval for proposed additions or removals does not change the required and conditional answer layers established in the same source message.
The AI chapter was explicitly authorized and its topic, format, inclusion status, and length guidance remain unchanged by the approval gate.
The approval workflow does not alter the client-approved chapter's audience, leadership-specific focus, format, or length guidance.

This Requirement already concerns reviewing and recommending question or category changes; the separate approval gate governs implementation without changing its coverage, criteria, or recommendation options.
The modernization actions remain recommendations for additions, categories, and rewording; editorial approval before implementation does not alter those modernization objectives or actions.
The broadened approval gate does not change the Google Doc, suggesting-mode, tracked-edit, or deletion-rationale requirements.
The source decision does not change how the global perspective is integrated, its introductory note, or its target markets.
The approval rule for author-proposed revisions or additions does not necessarily change the already requested companion-resource package or its delivery expectations.
